verdict: MSCI's revenue rose 12% to $892M as rising markets lifted the fees it earns on index-linked funds, and it kept $351M of it — a 39-cent profit on every dollar.

kpis.label: Operating margin
kpis.note: among the highest of any large public company

kpis.label: Index revenue
kpis.note: +18% — asset-based fees rode the market rally

segments.name: Index
segments.note: Licensing stock and bond indexes (the MSCI World and Emerging Markets benchmarks) to fund managers. Much of the fee floats with the value of assets in index funds — so a rising market raises MSCI's revenue automatically.

segments.name: Analytics
segments.note: Risk and portfolio analytics subscriptions sold to asset managers and banks.

segments.name: ESG & Climate
segments.note: Sustainability ratings and climate data for investors.

segments.name: All Other — Private Assets
segments.note: Data and analytics for private markets — real estate, private equity and infrastructure.

opex.name: Selling and marketing
opex.note: Selling subscriptions and index licenses worldwide.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building indexes, models and data products.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Write-down of assets bought in past acquisitions.

opex.name: Depreciation & other amortization
opex.note: Wearing-out cost of equipment and offices.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $75M on MSCI's debt, less $3M of interest income, plus $2M of other expense.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: The market does MSCI's selling
takeaways.text: Index revenue jumped 18%: $49M of the quarter's $99M revenue increase came from asset-based fees, which rise automatically when markets lift the value of index-tracking funds.

takeaways.title: A toll-booth margin
takeaways.text: Once an index or dataset exists, serving one more customer costs little — hence a 56.3% operating margin and $39 of every $100 kept as profit after interest and tax.

takeaways.title: Buybacks shrink the share count
takeaways.text: Diluted shares fell to 72.3M from 76.6M a year ago — buybacks are why EPS grew 14% on 8% net income growth.

footerNote: Figures are rounded to whole $M from the release's one-decimal presentation, with $1M of rounding absorbed in Index segment revenue.
